newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Red Cross seeks access to trapped Sierra Leoneans.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross seeks access to trapped Sierra Leoneans.

text.p: The Red Cross said on Thursday it was trying to get access to civilians trapped south east of Sierra Leone's capital after fighting between Nigerian troops and soldiers loyal to the military junta.

International Committee of the Red Cross delegate Rene-Luc Thevoz told Reuters that the Red Cross had urged the two sides to let it take in food and medicine and treat any wounded after last weekend's fighting around nearby Jui.

"We are not sure how many people are trapped in Kossoh Town but we know there are several hundred of them and possibly even several thousands," he said. "We are also strongly considering an evacuation of the civilians."

Sierra Leone's neighbours denounced a May 25 coup and opted in Guinea on June 26 for dialogue and economic sanctions to persuade the junta to restore ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah to power. They retained the military option.

Nigeria, which had troops in Sierra Leone before the coup under a defence pact, has since reinforced its presence. Its forces have clashed several times with soldiers supporting the coup and their Revolutionary United Front rebel allies.
Ghana and Guinea also have troops in Sierra Leone under the same defence pact with Sierra Leone's neighbours.
